# M4 shell-retention replay

`m4-x7071.json`: completed b60 run, 114 tool calls, local source
`/tmp/pod-logs-0917/work/pod-tiel-coder-35b-a3b-mtp-d2-b60-64k-skills-X7071/M4-data-report-py-r1/`.
`m4-y8191.json`: completed b61 run, 72 tool calls, read-only snapshot from the
same run-directory pattern under `/root/.cache/invokr-marathon/work/` on the pod.
Neither fixture contains task content: only tool names, paths, argument/output
byte lengths, turn boundaries, and assistant prose lengths. Y8191's token trace
was not included in the initial extraction. Neither trace drives replay state.

Regenerate from accessible archives:

```sh
python3 agent/testdata/replay/extract-native.py RUN_DIRECTORY > fixture.json
go test ./agent -run '^TestM4ShellReplayHeadroom$' -count=1 -v
```

The replay runs production admission gating, shell write capability,
retention, and compaction with a fixed 1,600-byte summary. The window is 61,440
effective tokens, plus the existing replay's 5,422-token fixed prompt overhead.
Tool bodies are size proxies, not literal content; previews and tokenization are
therefore approximations. This cannot predict scores or reproduce the exact
number/timing of live compactions. A different prompt changes subsequent model
behavior, which a fixed transcript deliberately cannot simulate.

Two density settings exercise that uncertainty. 1.4 is the older M3 replay fit.
X7071's data-heavy turns before its first compaction have engine growth divided
by gated `bytes/4` growth around 2.6–2.8 (turns 9–13); 2.6 tests this regime.
The fit is not transferred to Y8191 as a measured parameter: there it is a
sensitivity check. Historical token calibration absorbs prompt overhead too.

At dev b4c593e, with the same admission gate and replay:

| Fixture / density | Compactions | Longest consecutive | Peak after compaction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| X7071 / 1.4 | 6 | 1 | ~41.3k |
| X7071 / 2.6 | 35 | 24 | ~59.7k |
| Y8191 / 1.4 | 1 | 1 | ~25.7k |
| Y8191 / 2.6 | 4 | 1 | ~38.1k |

With recoverable payload reduction and bounded paired pins: X7071 becomes
3/8 compactions, streak 1, peak ~18.6k/~31.4k; Y8191 becomes 1/3, streak 1,
peak ~18.8k/~26.3k. Temp archive path lengths can move byte estimates slightly.
The regression asserts no streak over two and post-compaction occupancy under
60%, rather than pinning incidental counts. Y8191's live streak is not exactly
reproduced; X7071 establishes the storm mechanism and red-before/green-after.

The older ungated M3 replay's `m3-head558` baseline moves from two compactions
to one because the aggregate pin budget lowers its retained floor. Other M3
baselines are unchanged. This is not evidence of any benchmark-score change.

Prefetch regression: `TestCompactionArchivesWithoutDiscardingPrefetch` fails at
c0ed5ce with two summary calls and passes after resolving the original segment
before archival (one call). Both normal and over-window compaction must reuse
a covering prefetch. Archive rewriting also clears stale typed content blocks
so providers projecting those blocks cannot retain the old large payload.
